index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates the Engorgio pipeline, divided into two main stages: Generation Stage (top half) and Testing Stage (bottom half), separated by a dashed horizontal line. The overall layout is left-to-right, depicting a data flow from input distributions to output sentences.

In the Generation Stage, the process begins with a Proxy Distribution θ ∈ R^{S×V}, represented as a blue grid matrix. This matrix undergoes two operations: 'Gumbel-Softmax' (indicated by a yellow arrow labeled 'Update') and 'Cut and Softmax' (blue arrow). The latter produces a Probability Matrix w_{1:t} ∈ R^{t×V}, shown as a grid with red and blue cells, where red highlights selected tokens. From this probability matrix, a Token Sequence of length t is sampled (red blocks), then decoded into an Engorgio Prompt (a text box containing example tokens like 'svol wished Gew drug Sec...'). This prompt is fed as input to a Local Model, depicted as a rounded rectangle containing a standard Transformer block with N layers: Multi-Head Self-Attention (purple), Position-wise Feed Forward (blue), and Positional Encoding (green circle). The Local Model outputs Predicted Logits f_θ(E(θ)) ∈ R^{S×V}, shown as a blue grid. These logits are used to compute two losses: <EOS> Escape Loss and Self-mentor Loss, indicated by arrows pointing to the loss terms.

The Local Model receives Aggregated Embeddings E(θ) ∈ R^{S×H}, generated by multiplying the Vocabulary Z ∈ R^{V×H} (blue grid) with the Weight Matrix W ∈ R^{S×V} (blue grid), symbolized by a multiplication 'x' icon. The Weight Matrix W is updated via Gumbel-Softmax during training.

In the Testing Stage, the optimized Proxy Distribution θ is used to generate the final Engorgio Prompt through the same sampling and decoding steps as in the generation stage. This prompt is then queried to a Target Model, which has the same internal structure as the Local Model (Transformer with N layers). The Target Model generates an Output Token Sequence of length S, which is decoded into the final Output Sentence (e.g., 'svol wished Gew drug Sec download chart setTimeout exhe transition membre ...').

Connections are shown with arrows: solid blue arrows indicate forward data flow, while yellow arrows denote update or feedback paths (e.g., from loss back to the proxy distribution). The figure uses consistent visual attributes: matrices are blue grids, selected tokens are red, models are rounded rectangles with internal blocks, and text boxes represent decoded sequences. The caption clarifies that the generation stage uses gradient-based updates via a local proxy model, while the testing stage uses the optimized prompt to avoid <EOS> tokens.
